common_meaning: Perhaps; possibly; used to show uncertainty or to make a suggestion softer.
example: Maybe we should leave early to beat the traffic.
rrgm_bridge: Maybe holds a possibility open without committing to it; it marks a claim as live but unweighed.
invariant_mi: Marks a proposition as possible but not asserted.

domain_entries.LIN: Hedging adverb; also softens requests and suggestions.
domain_entries.COG: Expresses uncertainty without a stated probability.

count_condition: A proposition the speaker holds as possible but does not assert.
transfer_boundary: Maybe is not a probability; it could mean anything from unlikely to probable. Used as a polite refusal ("maybe another time"), it may mean no.

common_meaning: The number 1,000,000; a thousand thousand; informally, a very large number.
example: The city has about two million people.
rrgm_bridge: A million is a count so large that it cannot be seen at once, only measured.
invariant_mi: The cardinal number ten to the sixth power.

domain_entries.FOR: 10^6. A unit of scale in counting, money and measurement.
domain_entries.ECO: Common scale for budgets, populations and sales.

count_condition: A quantity equal to one thousand thousand, or used loosely for "very many".
transfer_boundary: In everyday speech "a million" is often exaggeration ("a million times"), not a count. Large numbers are easy to misjudge; comparisons should keep the same scale.

common_meaning: A place where goods are bought and sold; also the whole system of buying and selling a kind of goods, or the demand for them.
example: There's a farmers' market every Saturday; the market for used cars is strong.
rrgm_bridge: A market is where offers meet demand and a price forms between them.
invariant_mi: A setting, physical or abstract, where buyers and sellers exchange and prices are set.

domain_entries.ECO: Supply, demand and competition set prices; markets can fail, through monopoly, missing information or costs pushed onto others.
domain_entries.REL: Markets rely on trust and rules about fair dealing; most are regulated.
domain_entries.DIG: Online marketplaces and app stores, where a platform controls access and takes a share.

count_condition: Buyers and sellers able to exchange, with prices that respond to them.
transfer_boundary: A market price is what something sells for, not what it is worth in every sense. "The market decided" names an outcome of many choices; it does not mean no one decided.

common_meaning: To promote and sell a product or service, especially through advertising.
example: They marketed the game mainly to teenagers.
rrgm_bridge: To market is to shape how a thing is seen so that people will want it.
invariant_mi: To present and promote something in order to sell it.

domain_entries.ECO: Marketing covers pricing, packaging, advertising and targeting particular buyers.
domain_entries.COG: Marketing works through attention, framing and association.

count_condition: A product or service and an effort to promote it to buyers.
transfer_boundary: Being well marketed is not the same as being good; the promotion and the product are judged separately.

common_meaning: Sounds organised in time, through rhythm, melody, harmony or timbre, made for expression or enjoyment; also the art of making them.
example: She plays music every evening after work.
rrgm_bridge: Music is pattern in sound that listeners can follow and anticipate, so that its turns can satisfy or surprise.
invariant_mi: Intentionally organised sound, structured in time, made or received as expression.

domain_entries.PHY: Vibration in air at frequencies and intervals; harmony follows ratios between frequencies.
domain_entries.COG: Listeners track rhythm and melody and form expectations, which music then fulfils or breaks.
domain_entries.AFF: Music can move listeners, evoking strong feelings. Parity line: whether a given system experiences music is [UNK] under the Symmetry Rule. Provisional domain.
domain_entries.REL: Shared music marks communities, rituals and identities.
domain_entries.MYT: Music of the spheres: the old idea that the cosmos is ordered by harmonic ratios.

count_condition: Sound organised in time by someone, or perceived by someone as organised.
transfer_boundary: What counts as music varies across cultures; a pattern being unfamiliar does not make it noise. Music can be generated by machines without settling whether the machine experiences it.

common_meaning: Reflexive and emphatic form of I or me.
example: I made it myself; I hurt myself on the step.
rrgm_bridge: Myself bends the action back onto the speaker, who is both actor and the one acted upon.
invariant_mi: The speaker, as object of their own action or for emphasis.

domain_entries.LIN: Reflexive pronoun ("I cut myself") and intensifier ("I did it myself").
domain_entries.COG: The grammar of self-reference: the speaker naming themselves as both subject and object.

count_condition: A sentence where the speaker refers back to themselves.
transfer_boundary: Using "myself" in place of "I" or "me" ("contact myself") is common but often judged nonstandard. Self-reference in grammar does not settle questions about the self.

common_meaning: To walk with regular steps, as soldiers do; also to walk in a group as a public protest; and a piece of music for marching.
example: Thousands marched to the parliament to demand change.
rrgm_bridge: Marching aligns many walkers into one rhythm, so a crowd moves and is seen as a single body.
invariant_mi: To walk in a regulated, collective, purposeful way, or a public procession of that kind.

domain_entries.REL: A protest march makes a group's demand visible in public space.
domain_entries.PHY: Regular step; soldiers break step on bridges because rhythmic loading can build resonance.

count_condition: A group or individual walking in regulated step or in organised procession.
transfer_boundary: The size of a march shows how many turned out, not whether their demand is right. "March" as a verb is not the month March (a proper noun).

common_meaning: Relating to soldiers or armed forces; also the armed forces of a country.
example: He served in the military for ten years.
rrgm_bridge: The military is a state's organised capacity for armed force, held under a chain of command.
invariant_mi: The armed forces of a state, or matters relating to them.

domain_entries.REL: Civilian control of the military is a basic safeguard in democracies.
domain_entries.ECO: Military spending is a large share of many national budgets.

count_condition: Armed forces or matters relating to them.
transfer_boundary: Military strength is not the same as security; the two are often confused. Obeying orders does not remove responsibility for what is done.

common_meaning: Relating to medicine, the treatment of illness, or doctors.
example: She needs medical attention.
rrgm_bridge: Medical marks the domain of care for the body's illness and injury.
invariant_mi: Relating to the practice of medicine.

domain_entries.BIO: Diagnosis and treatment of disease and injury.
domain_entries.FOR: Medical evidence comes from trials and records; its strength depends on method.

count_condition: A matter concerning health care or medicine.
transfer_boundary: A "medical" claim in advertising is not medical advice. Medical consensus can change with new evidence.

common_meaning: A film; a motion picture.
example: Let's watch a movie tonight.
rrgm_bridge: Movie is the everyday name for a film, from "moving picture".
invariant_mi: A motion picture.

domain_entries.LIN: Common in North American English; "film" is more common elsewhere.
domain_entries.REL: Shared viewing is a common social ritual.

count_condition: A motion picture, as watched for entertainment.
transfer_boundary: See film: a movie based on true events is still a constructed story.

common_meaning: The process of running and controlling something; also the people who do this.
example: Management announced the new schedule.
rrgm_bridge: Management keeps a structure working by deciding how its resources are used.
invariant_mi: The direction and control of an organisation or process, or those who do it.

domain_entries.ECO: Allocating people, money and time toward goals.
domain_entries.REL: "Management" as a group stands apart from the staff it directs, which can create distance.

count_condition: An activity of directing resources, or the group responsible for it.
transfer_boundary: "Managing" a problem can mean containing it rather than solving it.

common_meaning: A contest in which people or teams compete; also a person or thing equal to another, or a pair that fits together.
example: The match ended in a draw; the colours are a perfect match.
rrgm_bridge: A match pairs two things, whether as opponents or as fits.
invariant_mi: A pairing, as contest, equivalence or correspondence.

domain_entries.REL: A good match between people; "meeting your match" means meeting an equal.
domain_entries.DIG: A match in search or data is an item that meets the query.
domain_entries.FOR: Pattern matching tests whether items meet a specified form.

count_condition: Two sides in contest, or two things that correspond.
transfer_boundary: A search match meets the query terms; it is not necessarily relevant or correct.

common_meaning: A short stick tipped with a substance that ignites when struck.
example: She struck a match to light the candle.
rrgm_bridge: A match stores a small fire until friction releases it.
invariant_mi: A small stick that ignites by friction.

domain_entries.PHY: Friction heats the head until it ignites.

count_condition: A stick designed to ignite when struck.
transfer_boundary: A small source can start a large fire; scale of cause and effect need not match.

common_meaning: (North American, informal) Mother.
example: My mom picked me up from school.
rrgm_bridge: Mom is the warm, everyday name for a mother.
invariant_mi: An informal word for mother.

domain_entries.REL: A family role; what it involves varies between families.
domain_entries.LIN: "Mum" in British usage; "mom" in North America.

count_condition: A person's mother, named informally.
transfer_boundary: Motherhood is a relation, not only biology; adoptive and step-mothers are moms by relation.

common_meaning: Relating to the present or recent times; also using new ideas, methods or styles.
example: Modern medicine has extended lives.
rrgm_bridge: Modern marks the present period against what came before, a line that keeps moving.
invariant_mi: Of the present or recent era, or new in style or method.

domain_entries.REL: "Modern" is relative to the speaker's time; every age was modern once.

count_condition: Something of recent times or new design.
transfer_boundary: Modern is not automatically better; newness and improvement are separate.

common_meaning: A senior member of a government in charge of a department; also a member of the clergy.
example: The health minister announced new funding; the minister led the service.
rrgm_bridge: A minister is one who serves, whether a department of state or a congregation.
invariant_mi: A person who heads a government department or serves as clergy.

domain_entries.REL: Ministers answer to parliament or to their congregation.

count_condition: A government department head or a clergy member.
transfer_boundary: The word comes from Latin "servant"; the role's authority is meant to be in service.

common_meaning: Joined in marriage.
example: They got married last spring.
rrgm_bridge: Married names a bond made formal, recognised by law or community.
invariant_mi: In a state of marriage.

domain_entries.REL: Marriage creates legal and social ties; who may marry has changed over time.

count_condition: A person or couple in a marriage.
transfer_boundary: Being married is a legal and social status; it does not describe the relationship's quality.

common_meaning: A unit of distance equal to 1,760 yards (about 1.6 km).
example: The beach is two miles away.
rrgm_bridge: The mile is an old measure of walking distance, from the Roman thousand paces.
invariant_mi: A unit of length of 1.609 km.

domain_entries.FOR: Imperial unit; a nautical mile is longer (1.852 km).

count_condition: A distance of 1,760 yards.
transfer_boundary: A nautical mile is not a land mile.

common_meaning: A person responsible for running an organisation, department or team.
example: The manager approved the leave.
rrgm_bridge: A manager holds a part of a structure together, deciding how its people and resources are used.
invariant_mi: One who directs and is accountable for part of an organisation.

domain_entries.ECO: Managers allocate resources and answer for results.

count_condition: A person with responsibility for running a unit.
transfer_boundary: A manager directs work but does not do all of it; credit and blame should follow who did what.

common_meaning: The greater number or part; more than half; also the age at which one becomes a legal adult.
example: The majority voted yes.
rrgm_bridge: A majority is the larger share, which in voting decides what happens.
invariant_mi: More than half, or the larger part.

domain_entries.REL: Majority rule decides; minority rights limit what it may decide.
domain_entries.FOR: Simple majority (more than half) versus plurality (the largest share).

count_condition: The larger part of a group, or legal adulthood.
transfer_boundary: The majority decides what happens, not what is true. A plurality is not a majority.

common_meaning: A person with control or authority over others; also someone highly skilled; also an original copy; as a verb, to learn fully.
example: A master carpenter; she mastered French.
rrgm_bridge: Master names command over people, over a craft, or over a copy from which others are made.
invariant_mi: One with control or full skill, or an original.

domain_entries.REL: Master–servant relations; the word's history includes slavery.
domain_entries.COG: Mastery: skill developed to a high level.
domain_entries.DIG: "Master" branch naming in software has largely shifted to "main".

count_condition: A person with authority or skill, an original, or the act of mastering.
transfer_boundary: Mastery of one craft does not transfer automatically to others.

common_meaning: The legally or formally recognised union of two people as partners; also a close combination of things.
example: Their marriage lasted fifty years.
rrgm_bridge: Marriage makes a partnership formal, so that law and community recognise it.
invariant_mi: A recognised union of partners, or a close combination.

domain_entries.REL: Marriage laws have changed widely, including who may marry.
domain_entries.ECO: Marriage carries legal and financial consequences.

count_condition: A recognised partnership, or a combining of elements.
transfer_boundary: The legal form does not describe the relationship within it.

common_meaning: An important task, often involving travel; also a group sent to do it; also a strong sense of purpose; also a religious centre.
example: A rescue mission; the company's mission.
rrgm_bridge: A mission is a sending-out toward a purpose.
invariant_mi: An assigned purpose or the group sent to carry it out.

domain_entries.REL: Religious missions spread faith, with complex histories in colonised places.
domain_entries.ECO: Mission statements set an organisation's stated purpose.

count_condition: A task with purpose, or those sent to do it.
transfer_boundary: A stated mission is a claim; conduct shows the actual one.

common_meaning: The crime of deliberately and unlawfully killing a person; as a verb, to commit this crime.
example: He was charged with murder.
rrgm_bridge: Murder is the law's gravest name for one person taking another's life.
invariant_mi: The unlawful, deliberate killing of a person.

domain_entries.REL: The most serious crime in most legal systems.
domain_entries.FOR: Distinguished in law from manslaughter by intent.

count_condition: An unlawful killing with intent.
transfer_boundary: Guilt is for courts to establish; an accusation is not a finding. Informal uses ("murder a song") are hyperbole.

common_meaning: Able to move or be moved easily; as a noun, a mobile phone, or a hanging decoration.
example: Call me on my mobile; mobile libraries.
rrgm_bridge: Mobile marks capacity to move, of people, devices and things.
invariant_mi: Capable of moving, or a mobile phone.

domain_entries.ECO: Social mobility: moving between economic positions.

count_condition: Something able to move, or a mobile phone.
transfer_boundary: Social mobility on average can hide groups that are stuck.

common_meaning: Relating to the mind; also (informally, offensive) mad.
example: Mental health matters.
rrgm_bridge: Mental names the domain of the mind.
invariant_mi: Of the mind.

domain_entries.BIO: Mental health and illness have biological and social sides.
domain_entries.PEJ: Informally used as an insult meaning crazy; the mechanism uses mental illness as a put-down.

count_condition: Something relating to the mind, or (informally) a slur.
transfer_boundary: Mental illness is health, not character; using it as an insult adds stigma.

common_meaning: Mainly; for the most part; usually.
example: The audience was mostly students.
rrgm_bridge: Mostly names the larger share, leaving room for the rest.
invariant_mi: For the greater part.
count_condition: A majority share or most occasions.
transfer_boundary: Mostly is not all; the remainder can matter.
